targets.authors: Ramer, N. E., Perhamus, G. R., & Colder, C. R.
targets.title: Reinforcement sensitivity theory and externalizing problems across early adolescence: Testing within-person reciprocal associations.
targets.evidence_quote:
This study is a replication of Ramer et al., using a comparable
                                                                                                                                   Norwegian nonclinical sample of preadolescents (N = 2,147) with ﬁve annual measurement occasions.
targets.outcome_quote:
We replicated associations between increased BAS sensitivity and
                                                                                                                                   subsequent increases in oppositional problems (i.e., vulnerability effect), and increased conduct problems
                                                                                                                                   with subsequent decreases in BIS sensitivity (i.e., scar effect). This could indicate that oppositional and
                                                                                                                                   conduct problems are inﬂuenced by different temperamental dispositions. We did not replicate oppositional
                                                                                                                                   problems inﬂuencing BAS sensitivity or BIS sensitivity inﬂuencing conduct problems.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly confirm BAS predicting oppositional problems and conduct problems predicting BIS, while failing to confirm the reverse directions. These are partly supporting and partly nonreplicating comparisons of the target.

reasoning: Secondary analysis uses independently collected Norwegian data to retest the U.S. Ramer et al. (2024) findings, so this is a replication despite using existing data. The Norwegian effectiveness-study publications provide the data source rather than findings retested here. No reanalysis of the original American dataset is reported.
